prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can you recommend a white wine from Greece that is a little sweet, and maybe made by a small family vineyard? I'm curious and want to try something new."

List A:
Wine 1: Moschofilero, Greece, $19. Tasting note: "Elegant white rose and peach aromas lead this delicate white from Greece. Fresh peach, grapefruit and delicate spice on the palate give the wine pretty poise. Overall, a great example of how refined the Greek wines can be."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, Greece, $15. Tasting note: "Fresh lemon and banana aromas lead this curvy white from Greece. Pineapple and citrus flavors are balanced by a touch of spice. Overall the wine is a commercial, friendly-style Chardonnay for fans of easy-drinking whites."
Wine 3: Chardonnay, Greece, $17. Tasting note: "Aromas of pineapple, orange and lemon lead this fruity and fun Chardonnay from Greece. Balanced fresh fruit flavors are lifted by a good acidity and spice. Easy to love and offering an international style, this is a white wine for the weekday as well as weekend."
Wine 4: Moschofilero, Greece, $16. Tasting note: "Vanilla, citrus and white flowers on the nose lead this memorable white from mainland Greece. The overall character is linear and crisp, with lemon and limestone flavors interlaced with exotic fruits and rose. A wine with class and character that will offer diverse food pairing experiences."
Wine 5: Xynisteri, Cyprus, $16. Tasting note: "This Cypriot white has a rich, lemony nose and on the palate, a delicate array of white and yellow fruit. The finish is crisp and clean, but overall, the wine has some weight. A good everyday white made from an ancient grape."

List B:
Wine 1: White Blend, Greece, $22. Tasting note: "A sophisticated, delicate nose of fresh flowers, peach, lemon and spice leads this attractive wine from Greece. On the palate, crisp flavors of lemon, minerals and spice dominate. Refreshing and clean, it will pair well with Asian food, seafood, salads."
Wine 2: Moschofilero, Greece, $19. Tasting note: "Elegant white rose and peach aromas lead this delicate white from Greece. Fresh peach, grapefruit and delicate spice on the palate give the wine pretty poise. Overall, a great example of how refined the Greek wines can be."
Wine 3: Muscat, Greece, $13. Tasting note: "Orange peel, spice and lemon aromas start this Muscat out with spirit. On the palate, vanilla, toasted nut and lemon/orange flavors create a very pretty and balanced white. The wine finishes clean and crisp. An elegant choice that reflects the refined minerality for which Greece is known."
Wine 4: Chardonnay, Italy, $38. Tasting note: "Here is a quintessentially luminous and fragrant white wine from southern Italy (made with 100% Chardonnay, two thirds of which was aged in oak) that delivers food-friendly appeal, succulence and a sophisticated approach. The wine is thick and luscious on the palate and offers slightly sweet flavors of exotic fruit, mango and papaya."
Wine 5: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $20. Tasting note: "It's rare to get a white wine from Cabernet-centric Rutherford, but Voss does a good job with this dry, crisp, low-alcohol Sauvignon Blanc. You can taste the coolness of the vintage in the tangy acidity and the gooseberry-accented citrus, fig and white pepper flavors."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
